questions.q: What is the capstone project built around?
options: A random open-source project with no connection to the course
Northbridge Retail's storefront-api, a small containerized REST API with tests and a Dockerfile
A purely theoretical pipeline that is never actually run
A spreadsheet tracking deployment dates
questions.explain: The capstone centers on storefront-api, a small, realistic containerized service for Northbridge Retail, chosen to be modest but representative of real pipeline patterns.

questions.q: Which of the following is one of the six requirements for the finished capstone pipeline?
options: Deploy directly to production with no testing at all
Require manual approval before deploying to production, while staging deploys automatically
Never build a container image
Skip triggers entirely and run the pipeline manually every time
questions.explain: The pipeline should auto-deploy to staging (Continuous Deployment) but require manual approval for production (Continuous Delivery) — reflecting the mixed pattern taught in Chapter 1.

questions.q: According to the lesson, if you're short on time, what should you cut FIRST?
options: The automated test step
The production approval gate — deploy straight to staging only
The entire Dockerfile
The pull request trigger
questions.explain: The suggested order of cuts is: production approval gate first, then GitOps, then the registry push — with automated tests never cut under any circumstance.

questions.q: Why should the automated test step never be cut, even under time pressure?
options: Because tests are the easiest part to write
Because a CI/CD pipeline with no tests doesn't demonstrate the core skill the course taught
Because GitHub Actions requires at least one test to run at all
Because tests are optional in real production pipelines
questions.explain: Automated testing is central to CI/CD's value — a pipeline that skips it isn't really demonstrating continuous integration or safe continuous delivery/deployment.

questions.q: What are the three deliverables expected by the end of Lesson 30?
options: A PowerPoint deck, a budget, and a hiring plan
A working repository with Dockerfile and tests, one or two pipeline YAML files, and a short written note on the deployment strategy chosen
Only a verbal description of the pipeline with no code
A fully staffed Ops team
questions.explain: The deliverables are a working repo (with Dockerfile and test suite), the pipeline YAML file(s) implementing the required stages, and a short note explaining the deployment strategy choice.
